newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Sihanouk denies role in royalist woes.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk denies role in royalist woes.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk on Thursday denied creating problems for his son's royalist party and urged a dissident party official to put an end to rumours the king was meddling in politics.

In a letter to Ton Chhay, who is leading a breakaway faction of co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, Sihanouk asked the dissident leader to make clear that the monarch was not involved in the party split.

"I would like his excellency (Ton Chhay) and his wife to write a letter to me and my wife (Queen Norodom Monineath) as soon as possible to tell the truth about FUNCINPEC and Prince Norodom Ranariddh," Sihanouk said in a letter from Beijing where he is recovering from an eye operation.

Ton Chhay last month condemned Ranariddh's leadership of the royalist party and started his own faction of FUNCINPEC in a move that raised political tensions between Ranariddh and co-Premier Hun Sen, and led to a flurry of finger-pointing.
Hun Sen, who shares power with Ranariddh in an uneasy coalition government formed in 1993, said he supported Ton Chhay's faction, raising the ire of Ranariddh.
But Hun Sen denied Ranariddh's accusation that he engineered the split to weaken FUNCINPEC ahead of national elections next year, when the two leaders will likely oppose each other.
The king has also denied a role in the split.
An aide to Ton Chhay, who is governor of the northwest province of Siem Reap, said Ton Chhay had responded to the king's letter but would not comment further.
